name: Video Prototyping
description:
Video prototyping uses recorded or edited video to represent how a proposed product, service or interaction might work in context. People, props, interfaces and environments can be combined to simulate functionality that does not yet exist.

Video is particularly effective for representing interactions involving movement, time, multiple devices or changing environments.
whenToUse: Use video prototyping when an experience is difficult to communicate through static sketches and when implementing the underlying technology would be unnecessary or expensive at the current stage.
steps: Define the interaction or question to represent.
Decide what can be performed, mocked up or simulated.
Edit only enough to communicate the interaction clearly.
Review the video with collaborators or participants.
Use feedback to revise the concept before implementation.
lookOutFor: Video can make an unbuilt concept appear more complete and feasible than it really is.
Clearly distinguish simulated behaviour from functioning technology.
Avoid investing heavily in production quality when the concept itself remains uncertain.

resources.citation: Mackay, W. E. (1988). “Video Prototyping: A Technique for Developing Hypermedia Systems.” *CHI '88*.
Tomitsch, M. et al. (2021). *Design. Think. Make. Break. Repeat*. BIS Publishers.
